game: CLE@NYJ Week 10 2025, kickoff 2025-11-09 13:00 ET, outdoor, NYJ +1.5, total 37.5

script.base: Books have a near pick'em slog: NYJ +1.5, total 37.5, implied CLE 19.5 / NYJ 18.0 (nflverse closing line; pro-edge inputs). Neither side is priced to blow it open, so both lead backs stay on the field, but there are not enough points for a pass-volume game. CLE's weeks 6-8 identity is Quinshon Judkins (46 carries, 139 yards) with D.Gabriel inefficient when pressured; NYJ's is Breece Hall (51/230) plus J.Fields' 21 designed runs. Pace stays low and explosives, not sustained drives, decide it.
script.flip1: CLE leads by 10+ and clocks it. Judkins' carries jump toward 20 and the rush-under 82.5 dies, while Hall's carries dry up and his rush-under gets safer. D.Gabriel does not need to throw, so Jeudy/Fannin/Njoku yardage stalls.
script.flip2: NYJ grabs the lead or two explosives force a chase. Hall's carry count rises and the 70.5 under is in trouble; CLE abandons balance so Judkins' carries fall (his under gets safer) and air-yard targets (Jeudy 191 air yards in weeks 6-8, Bond's vacated 131 air yards) finally hit NYJ's right-side 8.26 YPA.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game report (nflverse), not inactives: CLE T Cornelius Lucas Out (back) — pressure up, rush efficiency down, more quick throws to RB/TE, deep WR yards down. CLE WR Isaiah Bond Out (foot) — he had 9 targets but only 9 yards on 131 air yards in weeks 6-8, so the vacancy is empty air yards more than production; next men are Jeudy (19 tgt/60 yds), Fannin (23/179) and Njoku (11/65), plus J.Thrash (8/67). CLE TE Harold Fannin Jr. Questionable (hamstring) — if limited, Njoku/Jeudy/Sampson absorb; if full, he remains the target engine. CLE LB Carson Schwesinger Questionable (ankle) — if he sits, NYJ run fit and TE/RB catches get easier. NYJ WR Garrett Wilson Questionable (knee) and only 8 targets/13 yards in weeks 6-8 — if he sits or is capped, Mason Taylor (14 tgt/67 yds), Josh Reynolds (12/54/185 air) and T.Johnson (9/124) are the funnel; lines have no saved reprice. NYJ G Xavier Newman-Johnson Questionable (ankle) — if out, Hall's efficiency dips. NYJ RB Khalil Herbert Questionable (groin) — Hall already had 51 of the recent carries; Allen is not in the weeks 6-8 rush leader list. NYJ LB Francisco Mauigoa Questionable (concussion) — if out, CLE TE/RB checkdowns (Fannin, Sampson, Ford) face a backup. Final inactives ~90 minutes pre-kick are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack, so shell is unknown (step limitation). Usable splits are location YPA and blitz only.
matchup.pressure: NYJ blitzes 31%; CLE EPA/db is -0.39 vs blitz and -0.22 vs no blitz (pack, 8-game/season sample as given). Pressure is a real CLE problem and should kill deep WR yards while boosting RB/TE checkdowns. CLE blitzes only 25%; NYJ EPA/db is -0.03 vs blitz and -0.03 vs none, so blitzing Fields/NYJ does not change their down-to-down output.
matchup.bleeds: NYJ defense (8 games): rush 4.79 YPC, 28 runs of 10+, 23 passes of 20+ for 247 yards; YPA left 6.8 (88 att), middle 4.75 (44), right 8.26 (104). They bleed outside, especially right, and are soundest in the middle; the run front is soft and explosive. CLE defense (8 games): rush 3.84 YPC, only 19 runs of 10+, 26 passes of 20+ for 248; YPA left 6.71 (85), middle 9.5 (28), right 7.13 (111). CLE's run front is the strength; the pass defense bleeds the middle on a small sample and is ordinary outside.
matchup.overlap: CLE's top option, Fannin (23 targets), works the intermediate/TE area, which is NYJ's best zone (middle 4.75 YPA) — bad overlap, and he is questionable. Jeudy (19 targets, 191 air, 60 yards) is the outside air-yard WR into the side NYJ actually bleeds (right 8.26) but he is not converting, and the 31% blitz cuts against him. The clean negative overlap is Hall, the NYJ primary runner (51 carries, 4.51 YPC in weeks 6-8), into CLE's 3.84 YPC front. Judkins has the carry share into a weak NYJ run front, but 15.3 carries times 4.79 YPC is still only about 73, short of 82.5.

form: Avoiding season averages as the decider. CLE weeks 6-8: Judkins 46/139 (3.02 YPC, ~15.3 carries, ~46 yards/game) after a last4 rush line of 110, 36, 84, 19 — the 110 is the older spike; recent three sum to 139. Sampson 9/20 rush and 9 targets/50 rec yards; Ford 3/17 rush and 10 targets/22 rec yards; Judkins receiving last4 18, 0, 0, -2 so he is not the pass-down back. Fannin weeks 6-8 yards 81/36/62 (179 total) vs a 42.5 median; Jeudy 43/17/0 type recent cluster (60 yards on 19 targets/191 air); Njoku 11 targets/65 yards, last4 11, 67, 28, 37. NYJ weeks 6-8: Hall 51/230 (59, 38, 133 shape — one explosive inflates a 76.7 mean; two of three under 70.5), Fields 21/85, I.Davis 11/77. Wilson 8 targets/13 yards in that window vs last4 rec yards 84, 82, 71, 13 and a 76.5 median — role has collapsed while knee is questionable. Mason Taylor weeks 6-8 look like 2, 31, 34 (67 yards on 14 targets). Reynolds 12 targets/54 yards/185 air. Allen last4 rush 9, 11, 30, 26 but not in the weeks 6-8 rush leader group.

pro_edge.script_read: Both implied totals under 20 and a 1.5 spread are a defensive slog, not a shootout. Spread is inside 3.5, so the dog is not forced into a pass-heavy chase in the base script; blowout flag is off, so starter snaps should hold unless a flip hits. Low total means fewer plays: lean efficiency unders and run-game caps, not WR yardage overs. Leader-runs-late only matters if someone actually leads.

Treat those gaps as unconfirmed lag, not as a bettable CLV number.
pro_edge.sleepers: Ruled out: CLE T Cornelius Lucas (back), CLE WR Isaiah Bond (foot). Questionable, not Out/IR, so not full sleeper triggers: Fannin (hamstring), Schwesinger (ankle), Herbert (groin), Newman-Johnson (ankle), Wilson (knee), Mauigoa (concussion). If Wilson sits, same-position lines with no saved move are Reynolds recyds 25.5 and Wilson's own 76.5; Mason Taylor 25.5 is the middle beneficiary with both LBs questionable. Bond's 9/9/131 does not hand a proven yardage bump to a teammate. Herbert Q would point at Allen/Davis, but Hall still had 51 carries and Allen is absent from the weeks 6-8 rush leaders. No prices moved in the saved file.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Breece Hall's 17-carry weeks 6-8 role runs into a Browns front allowing 3.84 YPC and only 19 runs of 10-plus in eight games, which projects about 65 rush yards against a 70.5 season-median line, with J.Fields already taking 21 carries in that same three-game window.
edge_players.must_be_true: Hall stays the lead back but not a 22-carry clock-killer, CLE's 3.84 YPC run defense shows up, Schwesinger is not a full scratch that guts the fit, and Newman-Johnson's ankle does not flip into a sudden efficient NYJ ground game. Base script stays within a score.
edge_players.kills_it: NYJ leads and feeds Hall 20-plus carries, or he repeats the 133-yard explosive game; Schwesinger sits and the 3.84 YPC mark does not travel; a late NYJ clock-kill the 1.5 spread does not currently price.

script.source: Implied NYJ 18.0 in a 37.5 total, spread only +1.5, so base script is competitive and low-play, not a Hall 25-carry blowout. CLE-leads flip also cuts his carries. Survives base and flip1; dies on flip2.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Quinshon Judkins has been a 15-carry, 46-yard back over weeks 6-8, and even granting him the Jets' generous 4.79 YPC he projects near 73 against an 82.5 season-median line, with tackle Cornelius Lucas out further capping efficiency.
edge_players.must_be_true: Carry share stays near 15, not 22; Lucas' absence or just his recent 3.02 YPC keeps him from a 5-plus YPC day; CLE does not turn a small lead into a 25-carry clock kill. He remains the RB1 (Sampson only 9 carries in the window).
edge_players.kills_it: NYJ's soft run front shows up as explosives — 28 runs of 10+ and 4.79 YPC in eight games — and Judkins stacks two or three of those on 18-plus carries in a CLE lead, the same path as his 110- and 84-yard games. A late Lucas active or a Schwesinger-style absence on the other side does not apply; the kill is purely NYJ run-defense generosity plus script.

data_check.notes: No projection file, no sims, no Pinnacle/Circa/BetOnline no-vig in the pack. model_p values (Hall 0.56, Judkins 0.60) are hand estimates from carry rate times opponent YPC, not a simulator, and both are kept under 0.65 because RB rush variance is wide and past calibration punished 70%+ tags. Judkins form agrees (46.3 vs 82.5) and the matchup-adjusted 73 is still under, but NYJ's 4.79 YPC and 28 explosive runs disagree with a clean under — that tension is why this card is flagged, not confirmed. Wilson 76.5, Fannin 42.5 and Jeudy 30.5 were considered and not carded: Wilson knee Q plus last4 84/82/71/13 conflicts with the 8-target/13-yard window; Fannin form (59.7) fights the middle-of-field under and the hamstring fights the over; Jeudy 20 yards on 191 air fits an under but he attacks the side NYJ bleeds (right 8.26). No prices, so nothing is sized.

Judkins rushyds under 82.5, no price, stand-in median of 7 games; rushrecyds 84.5 is almost the same bet given near-zero receiving and was not doubled. No alt rungs, no book, no CLV. Do not stake.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both unders lost. Hall ripped off the same explosive profile as his 133-yard game because Schwesinger sat and CLE's 3.84 YPC / 19 explosive-run sample did not travel to MetLife, finishing near 95 on 18 carries while Fields' 21 recent runs did not actually steal the goal-line work. Judkins got the weak Jets front the pack already shows (4.79 YPC, 28 runs of 10+), CLE led late, and 18 carries at 5 YPC plus one 20-yarder cleared 82.5 the way the 110 and the 84 already did this season — Lucas being out mattered less than the defensive generosity. A calm outdoor afternoon the missing forecast never ruled out also let both run games operate, and the 37.5 held as a competitive grind rather than a stuff-fest. The counter-case is strong enough that both legs stay leans, not strong, and the card stays flagged.
slip_story: One story only: outdoor low-total slog, both lines nicked (Lucas out, Newman-Johnson questionable), both lead backs miss their season-median rush lines because efficiency is capped and nobody is scripted for 22 carries. Slip is Hall rushyds under 70.5 plus Judkins rushyds under 82.5. They win together in the base script and each survives one flip; they lose together only if both fronts allow explosives. Do not add Wilson/Fannin/Jeudy/Taylor overs — those need a shootout or a confirmed inactive the report does not give. No TDs, no receptions, one market per player, two legs. Not a bet until inactives and a real price exist.
